Make it rain. Make Snow. Make Earth Habitable. 

Rainmaker builds and deploys audacious technologies that work with nature to create an abundant, habitable planet. We are modernizing proven cloud-seeding science with weather-resistant UAS, radar and satellite observations, numerical weather prediction, novel sensing and validation systems, and sustainable seeding technologies. We are building an integrated system to make more freshwater available to farms, ecosystems, and communities.

Our ambition is bold, but we pursue it with humility. We take on difficult problems in the real world with technical rigor, grit, integrity, and an openness to learning and course-correcting. We are hiring individuals with evidence of exceptional ability. If you want to build systems that endure, restore, and deliver the future we were promised, we want to hear from you.

 The vehicle software team builds the software that operates Rainmaker’s cloud-seeding vehicles, connecting flight control, onboard computing, sensors, payloads, and ground operations. We work closely with electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, and flight operations teams to turn new hardware into reliable systems that can be built, deployed, and operated at scale. Our goal is to make every vehicle a dependable tool for delivering more freshwater where it is needed.

About the Role

 - You will own vehicle software capabilities from the operator interface to the onboard systems that execute a mission. Your work will span ground stations, mission planning and execution, failsafe behaviors, sensing, payload and sensor integration, and autonomy. You will build software that helps operators make good decisions, lets vehicles carry out missions reliably, and handles failures predictably. You will take projects from architecture and prototyping through simulation, hardware integration, flight testing, deployment, and field support. We’re looking for a high-agency engineer who identifies what needs to happen, turns incomplete requirements into a clear plan, and follows through until the system works reliably in real operating conditions. This is a hands-on technical ownership role with the autonomy to shape the vehicle software and the responsibility to deliver it.

What You'll Do 

 - 

 - Own the architecture, implementation, and maintenance of vehicle software capabilities across onboard computers and ground systems, with clear contracts for commands, telemetry, state, and failure behavior.  

 - Build operator interfaces and ground-station workflows for vehicle preparation, preflight checks, mission control, health monitoring, and intervention. Make vehicle state, command outcomes, and required operator actions clear.  

 - Develop mission planning and execution software that turns operational goals into validated flight paths and geofences, accounts for vehicle endurance, coordinates flight and seeding activity, and supports mission changes as conditions evolve.  

 - Design and validate arming checks, interlocks, and failsafe behaviors for communication loss, degraded sensing, low power, process failures, and unexpected vehicle states, including clear transitions between autonomous behavior and operator control.  

 - Integrate sensors, cameras, and seeding payloads with onboard software and flight-control systems. Ensure measurements, calibration, timestamps, device health, and payload commands are reliable and observable.  

 - Develop autonomy that uses sensing and vehicle state to execute missions within operating limits, handle contingencies, and reduce operator workload.  

 - Build dependable communication between vehicles and ground stations, accounting for intermittent links, stale telemetry, and commands that may be delayed, duplicated, or unacknowledged.  

 - Build automated tests, software-in-the-loop simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop coverage that catch regressions and exercise failure modes before releases reach the fleet.  

 - Partner with hardware engineers and flight operations to validate new capabilities on the bench and in flight, and make deployment, configuration, calibration, and diagnostics repeatable.  

 - Investigate field failures using logs, telemetry, and mission replay; resolve root causes and turn what you learn into better software, tests, and operator workflows.

What We're Looking For

 - 

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience developing software for vehicles, robotics, or other systems that interact with the physical world, including deployment into production or field use.  

 - Demonstrated ownership of a software capability from design through integration, release, and ongoing support, including making technical decisions independently and resolving failures in real operating conditions.  

 - Strong systems programming skills in Rust or C/C++, with the willingness to work primarily in Rust and contribute to TypeScript-based operator interfaces. Our stack includes Rust onboard services and ground-station backends, React/TypeScript interfaces in Electron, and PX4 flight-control integration over MAVLink.  

 - Experience developing and debugging software on Linux, including concurrent processes, network communication, and interfaces to hardware or flight-control systems.  

 - Practical experience in one or more of the following: operator interfaces and ground stations, mission planning, autonomy, sensing, or payload integration, with the willingness to work across these boundaries.  

 - The ability to reason about distributed system state, timing, and failures, and implement robust state machines, fault detection, failsafes, and recovery paths.  

 - A practical approach to operator-facing software: you can turn field workflows into clear controls, useful feedback, and predictable system behavior.  

 - Experience building maintainable software with version control, reproducible builds, automated testing, and disciplined release practices.  

 - Evidence of high agency: you surface problems without waiting to be assigned, make sound decisions with incomplete information, ask for help when it matters, and close the loop on results.  

 - Clear communication and the ability to work closely with hardware engineers and operators, explain tradeoffs, and document decisions so others can operate and support what you ship.

What Will Set Your Apart

 - 

 - Experience deploying drones or autonomous robots and supporting real-world flight or field operations.  

 - Familiarity with PX4, MAVLink, ground-control systems, or flight-critical software.  

 - Experience building operator interfaces with React, TypeScript, or Electron, particularly mapping tools or geospatial mission-planning workflows.  

 - Experience with sensor fusion, state estimation, path planning, or autonomous mission execution.  

 - Experience integrating payloads, sensors, or embedded controllers over interfaces such as CAN, serial, or Ethernet.  

 - Experience validating safety-related behaviors through simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, fault injection, and field testing.

What Success Looks Like In the First 90 Days

 - You understand how operators plan and execute missions and can trace commands, telemetry, and failure behavior between the ground station, onboard software, flight controller, sensors, and payloads. You have identified the most consequential reliability risks and operator pain points, and the team has a clear plan for what to address first. You have delivered a meaningful vehicle software improvement through simulation and integration testing into an operational release, working with flight operations to verify its behavior in the field. You have demonstrated both its intended behavior and its response to relevant failures, and improved at least one recurring source of friction in mission planning, operation, testing, deployment, or diagnostics.

Supporting the Rainmakers behind the mission

Making earth more habitable is ambitious work and we want the people doing it to feel supported:

 - A stake in what we build: Meaningful stock options and the opportunity to help shape Rainmaker as an early member of the team. 

 - Support for your health: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your family. 

 - An investment in your future: A 401(k) with employer matching to help you build long-term savings. 

 - Time to recharge: Unlimited PTO for rest, exploration, and the people and pursuits that matter to you plus a generous paid holiday schedule. 

 - Time for a growing family: Paid parental leave for both parents to welcome a child and spend time together. 

 - Lunch together: Daily lunch provided at our El Segundo headquarters, giving Rainmakers a chance to share a meal and connect with teammates. 

 - Help making the move: Relocation assistance for eligible roles to support your transition to Rainmaker.

Software Engineer — AI Evaluation & Automation, 37928969
  
  
Role Overview
  
  
Help build and scale the tooling we use to measure how well AI-powered software development tools actually perform. You'll develop evaluation harnesses, automate benchmark runs, and help make sure the results we produce are reproducible and hold up to scrutiny. This is an engineering role, but a lot of the work is about getting the measurement right, not just automating it.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Build and integrate evaluation harnesses and automation for software development use cases, including turning real engineering artifacts like merged pull requests into repeatable benchmark tasks
* Build versioned, repeatable processes to evaluate AI tools, models, and harnesses, with reproducible run environments (pinned dependencies, containerized runs, isolated worktrees) so results stay comparable over time
* Validate and calibrate evaluation approaches against human judgment, so scores are consistent and correct rather than just repeatable
* Support execution-based benchmarking across quality, productivity, and efficiency measures, including cost and latency
* Analyze results across repeated runs, looking at variance, failure patterns, and cost per outcome, and find ways to make the workflows more reliable and more automated
* Work with engineering and data teams to improve the tooling, and document how the evaluations work and what they found for both technical and leadership audiences

**Required Skills & Experience**

* Strong software engineering background, with real experience building automation, developer tooling, or test and validation systems
* Proficient in at least one general-purpose language such as Python, Java, or JavaScript — the specific language background is flexible
* Solid working knowledge of Git, including how branches, history, and working trees behave, and of containerization with Docker
* Experience with APIs, development environments, CI/CD pipelines, and typical engineering workflows
* Understanding of how AI, LLM, or agent evaluation works and where it goes wrong, such as why a judge can be consistent but still wrong, why a single run can mislead, and how benchmark contamination happens
* Able to troubleshoot technical problems, think clearly about whether a measurement is valid, and analyze results carefully
* Hands-on experience using AI coding tools and agentic harnesses such as Claude Code, Devin, or Cursor, and command of the best practices for working with them effectively

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience designing benchmarks or evaluations for software systems, especially execution-based grading that verifies against tests
* Familiarity with LLM-as-judge or agent-as-judge approaches, and how to check them against human raters
* Experience with build-system-aware test selection, such as Bazel or mapping changed files to the tests that cover them
* Experience building reproducible test environments and managing versioned evaluation datasets
* Comfortable writing up methodology and results for engineering leadership

**Manager Notes**

* Based on the job description, what are the must have non-negotiable items that a candidate must have to be successful in this role?
* They must have experience using existing AI tools with harnesses such as Claude, Devin, Cursor etc. and the best practices using them
* Evaluation and benchmarking experience (getting the measurement right, not just automating it)
* Solid working knowledge of Git, including how branches, history, and working trees behave, and of containerization with Docker
* What backgrounds/skills can we be more flexible with that can be learned on the job?
* What is flexible is what coding languages they know, if they have built ML eval tools previously
* Does this position have the opportunity to extend beyond the initial contract or convert to FTE?
* Yes, the intention is to renew every 6 months, and if FTE positions become available contractors will be considered first
* Is there a specific laptop that needs to be used for this role (i.e. - Mac or Windows)?
* The company will provide the Mac
* Is there a required timezone?
* Remote but must work Pacific Time zone. Not accepting candidates with more than a two hour difference

$65.86–75.86/hr.

**About The Role**
The Machine Learning Server Software Team is seeking talented software engineers interested in developing data-driven software for our Machine Learning servers. This role focuses on building production software to initialize and monitor cutting-edge machine learning acceleration servers. You will work on technologies including accelerator chip initialization, clock and voltage settings, systems-level device drivers for I2C infrastructure, PCIe, SPI, and more. The team’s work centers around the physical hardware systems that execute and accelerate machine learning algorithms, rather than the algorithms themselves.
  
  
Key responsibilities include collaborating with hardware, test, and manufacturing teams to develop coordinated software packages that enable qualification and rapid deployment. You will develop maintainable, documented, and tested software primarily using C, C++, Python, and Lua. The role offers exposure to the full software development lifecycle and opportunities to contribute to scalable automation solutions that support organizational growth.
  
  
Our team values knowledge-sharing and mentorship, providing a supportive environment where senior members offer one-on-one mentoring and thorough code reviews. We are committed to your career development by assigning projects that enhance your engineering expertise and empower you to tackle complex challenges.
  
  
**Qualifications**

* 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
* 2+ years of design or architecture experience involving design patterns, reliability, and scaling of new and existing systems
* Proficiency in at least one software programming language (C, C++, Python, Lua preferred)
* Experience with the full software development lifecycle including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations (preferred)
* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or equivalent (preferred)

**Responsibilities**

* Develop, maintain, and improve software for server components and integration into EC2 environments
* Collaborate with MLA Hardware, Test, and Manufacturing teams to create coordinated software packages for qualification and deployment
* Write clean, documented, tested, and reusable code primarily in C, C++, Python, and Lua
* Support initialization, monitoring, debugging, testing, qualification, and manufacturing of machine learning acceleration servers
* Contribute to automation efforts to help scale organizational processes and software solutions
* Participate in code reviews and knowledge-sharing sessions to foster team growth and quality standards

**About The Team**
The Proactivity Research team, within OpenAI’s broader Post Training team, is focused on making our models in ChatGPT, Dots, and future potential products proactive in ways that are truly useful. We're laying the technical foundations for AI that can anticipate what users need in real time, adapt as their goals and preferences shift, and build a deeper, evolving understanding of the person it's helping.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Research Engineer / Scientist, you will research and develop improvements to our models’ personalization and agentic capabilities. Our team works on reinforcement learning, dataset creation, evaluations, and other post-training methods. We partner closely with research and product teams across the company to realize the vision of a highly personalized, collaborative, and proactive assistant.
  
  
We're looking for individuals with strong ML engineering skills and research experience, especially with novel and highly capable models. An ideal candidate is passionate about product-driven research.
  
  
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
  
  
**In This Role, You Will**

* Own and pursue a research agenda to improve the proactivity and ability of our models to anticipate user needs and further their goals.
* Build robust evaluations for tracking modeling improvements.
* Design, implement, test, and debug code across our research stack.
* Collaborate closely with the other research and product teams to influence the shape of technical solutions in the product

**You Might Thrive In This Role If You**

* Have a deep understanding of machine learning and machine learning applications.
* Have a working knowledge of LLM post-training and evaluation approaches
* Are passionate about, or have experience thinking about, personalization and enabling users to achieve their goals
* Are comfortable diving into a large ML codebase to debug.
* Thrive in a dynamic and technically complex environment.
